Yes — I typed "keyboard" and the list narrowed down right away to the one about accessible interface patterns, which is exactly the kind of instant filtering I was hoping for. Not having to hit a button and wait feels great, and it clearly looked inside the description, not just the title. I also tried a capital "Keyboard" and it still found it, which is what I'd want — I shouldn't have to worry about how I type it.

The sample bookmarks make sense for testing, and having search sit just under the save box that's always there works well for me.

One thing I want to flag while we're on search, since it's the same feature: titles and descriptions are the main thing, but there are two other places I'd naturally expect a search to look. One is the web address itself — sometimes I don't remember what a page was called, but I remember it was on a certain site, and I'd want typing that to find it. The other is for later: once I can jot my own notes on a bookmark, I'd expect a search to find words from those notes too. The description-and-title matching you've shown is right; I'd just want the net cast a little wider to include the address and, eventually, my notes. Can we make sure search covers those as well?
